question: What is the main job of surgical swabs during an operation?

options.A: Absorbing blood and clearing the surgical field
options.D: Measuring the patient's blood loss volume

explanation: You'll see these in every theatre! Surgical swabs are simple textile tools used to soak up fluids so the surgeon can clearly see what they are doing. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h1)

question: Why do nurses strictly track and count surgical swabs before closing a wound?

options.A: To prevent dangerous retained items inside the patient
options.B: To calculate the exact duration of the surgical procedure
options.C: To reduce the financial cost of hospital materials
options.D: To ensure the theater team finishes their shift early

explanation: Patient safety first! Counting every single swab ensures nothing is accidentally left behind inside the patient's body cavity. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h1)

question: Which type of surgical sponge is the largest and best for major tummy (abdominal) surgeries?
explanation: Lap sponges (laparotomy sponges) are large and heavy-duty, designed to handle deep abdominal operations easily. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h2)

question: What makes tonsil sponges different from standard gauze swabs?

options.A: They do not need to be counted during surgical operations
options.B: They are made entirely of synthetic plastic fibers
options.C: They are small and attached to strings for throat procedures
options.D: They are soaked in antibiotics before entering the theater

explanation: Because throat procedures are narrow, tonsil sponges come with attached strings so they can't accidentally slip down the airway! [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h2)

question: In the theatre team, who is mainly responsible for writing down the counts on the whiteboard?
explanation: The circulating nurse is outside the sterile field (unsterile zone), which makes them the perfect person to maintain the official tally board. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h3)

question: How should the scrub nurse and circulating nurse perform the swab counts?

options.A: By guessing the total based on how many packets opened
options.B: Out loud together in a synchronized manner
options.C: Silently by themselves to avoid disturbing the surgeon

explanation: Always count out loud together! It keeps everyone on the same page and prevents nasty miscount surprises. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h3)

question: When must the very first baseline swab count be done?

options.A: When the patient enters the recovery ward
options.B: After the surgical wound is closed
options.C: Only if an extra pack is requested

explanation: You have to know your starting point! The baseline count happens before any incision is made. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h4)

question: The surgeon is about to close the patient's tummy. What specific count must happen right now?
explanation: Before closing up deep spaces, a closure count is mandatory to double-check that no materials are trapped inside. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h4)

question: What special feature in modern surgical swabs helps find them easily on an X-ray?
explanation: Radiopaque strips show up brightly on X-ray machines, acting like a safety net if a swab ever goes missing. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is the very first thing the nursing team must do if a swab count doesn't add up?

options.A: Ignore the discrepancy if only one small gauze is missing
options.B: Discharge the patient and file an incident report later
options.C: Inform the surgeon immediately and halt closure
options.D: Wait until the patient wakes up to ask them

explanation: Never keep quiet about a wrong count! Alert the surgeon right away so nobody gets closed up with an extra item inside. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h5)

question: Leaving a surgical swab inside a patient is legally considered what kind of error?
explanation: It's a preventable mistake, which is why proper counting protocols are taken so seriously in nursing practice and law. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h6)

question: Why is keeping accurate records of swab counts so important for Nigerian nurses?

options.A: It provides legal protection and proves adherence to safety standards
options.B: It replaces the need to count out loud in the theater
options.C: It allows the hospital to buy fewer supplies next year
options.D: It is only required for hospital billing departments

explanation: Good paperwork is your best backup! Clear records show you followed all safety rules and protect you legally. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h6)

question: What should nurses do regarding swab counts during an emergency surgery?

options.A: Perform standard counts with heightened vigilance
options.B: Only count the lap sponges and ignore gauze
options.C: Skip the counts entirely to save precious time
options.D: Let the surgeon count the swabs alone

explanation: Emergencies are intense, but safety rules still apply! We stay extra alert during rushed situations to avoid mistakes. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to prevent leaving items inside a patient?

options.A: Rushing through the final count to finish quickly
options.C: Minimizing operating room noise during counts

explanation: Never rush a count! Taking your time, staying calm, and keeping the room quiet helps catch errors. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T7#GNS123_U5_T7_h7)
